name: City Council Meeting - Jul 02, 2024
agenda_text:
TORRANCE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  JULY 2, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING
  5:00 P.M. - CLOSED SESSION
  6:30 P.M. - REGULAR BUSINESS BEGINS
  AT THE TOYOTA MEETING HALL AT 3330 CIVIC CENTER DRIVE

  CITY COUNCIL MAY TAKE ACTION ON ANY ITEM LISTED ON THE AGENDA

Revised City Council Agenda 07-02-24

*Denotes the item was added after posting of the agenda.

OPENING CEREMONIES

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  ROLL CALL
  : Councilmembers Gerson, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Sheikh, and Mayor Chen

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  14A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION (California
  Government Code §54956.9(d)(1)):
  1)  City of Torrance v. Hi-Shear Corporation USDC Case No. 2:17-cv-07732-DSF-JPR
  2)  California Regional Water Quality Control Board Order No. R4-2020-0003 June 13,
  2020
  3)  California Regional Water Quality Control Board Order No. R4-2021-0079 June 18,
  2021
  14A - STAFF REPORT

  14B. REAL PROPERTY – CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR
  (California Government Code §54956.8):
  1)  Property: Hawthorne Boulevard from Pacific Coast Highway to north City limit Agency
  Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and California
  Department of Transportation (Caltrans) Under Negotiation: Price and terms and
  conditions of relinquishment
  2)  Property: 1520 Greenwood Avenue, Torrance, CA 90503 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and KinderCare Education LLC Under
  Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease
  3)  Property: 25341 Crenshaw Blvd, Torrance, CA 90505 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and AutoNation Acura South Bay
  Under Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease

  14C. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (California Government Code
  §54957.6): Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Employee
  Organization/Association:
  1. Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees
  2. Certain Part-Time Hourly Employees
  3. Crossing Guards
  4. Elected Officials
  5. Engineers and Torrance Fiscal Employees Association
  6. Executive & Management Employees
  7. Police & Fire Trainees
  8. Safety Management Employees
  9. Torrance City Employees Association
  10. Fire Safety Management
  11. Torrance Fire Fighters Association
  12. Torrance Library Employees Association
   13. Torrance Municipal Employees/AFSCME Local 1117 AFL-CIO
  14. Torrance Police Commanders Association (TPCA)
  15. Torrance Police Officers Association
  16. Torrance Professional Parks & Recreation Employees Organization
  17. Torrance Professional & Supervisory Association
  18. Torrance Recurrent Recreational Employees Organization
  19. City Treasurer
  20. City Attorney
  21. City Manager

  14D. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE (California Government
  Code §54957)

  14E. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION (California Government Code
  §54957(b)(1)): Title: City Attorney

RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION

RECONVENED IN PUBLIC SESSION

2.  FLAG SALUTE: Councilmember Sheikh

  NONSECTARIAN INVOCATION: Councilmember Gerson

3.  REPORT OF THE CITY CLERK ON THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA The agenda was
  posted on the Public Notice Board at 3031 Torrance Bl. and on the City’s Website on
  Tuesday, June 25, 2024 /s/ Rebecca Poirier
  3 - AFFIDAVIT
  3 - AFFIDAVIT REVISED

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READING OF RESOLUTIONS AND ORDINANCES AFTER
NUMBER & TITLE – See Council Rules of Order Section 2.11 (Resolution 2006-65)

4.  ANNOUNCEMENT OF WITHDRAWN, DEFERRED, AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL ITEMS

5.  COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

6.  COMMUNITY MATTERS

  6A. City Clerk – Appoint Members to Fill Commission Vacancies. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council review applications and appoint
  members to fill vacancies on various Commissions from a list of qualified applicants. The
  City Clerk will administer the Oath of Office to the newly appointed commissioners present.
  6A - STAFF REPORT

7.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #1 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comments on items under the Consent Calendar or items that
  are not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council cannot act on
  items raised during public comment, but may respond briefly to statements made or
  questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item to staff. Speakers under Orals
  are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral Communications #2 and no
  longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you step up to the microphone. If
  presenting handout material to Council, please provide 11 copies to the City Clerk
  before speaking. Handouts will be distributed while you speak.
  PUBLIC COMMENT

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..

  8A. City Clerk – Approve City Council Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council approve the City Council minutes of
   June 4, 2024, June 11, 2024, and June 18, 2024.

  8B. Community Development – Approve License Agreement for Use of Parking on
  City-Owned Property Located on Cravens Avenue Between 1511 and 1529
  Cravens Avenue. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council approve a
  license agreement with Gaburi Chicken USA Inc. of Torrance, CA for the use of six parking
  spaces on City-owned property located on Cravens Avenue between 1511 and 1529
  Cravens Avenue (APNs 7355-022-902 and 7355-022-903) for a five-year period beginning
  May 1, 2024 and ending on April 30, 2029, in conjunction with the operation of a restaurant
  located at 1437 Marcelina Avenue.
  8B - STAFF REPORT

  8C. Community Services – Accept and File 2023-2024 Torrance Rose Float
  Association Annual Report and Financial Statement. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council accept and file the
  2023-2024 Torrance Rose Float Association’s Annual Report and Financial Statement.
  8C - STAFF REPORT

  8D. Community Services – Authorize Parks and Recreation Commission to Conduct
  Regularly Scheduled Meeting at Charles H. Wilson Park. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council authorize the Parks
  and Recreation Commission to conduct the regularly scheduled meeting on July 10, 2024 at
  Charles H. Wilson Park.
  8D - STAFF REPORT

  8E.  Finance – Accept and File Projected Capital Improvement Project Procurements
  for Period Beginning June 1, 2024 and Ending December 31, 2024. Expenditure:
  None.
  Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council accept and file the projected
  Capital Improvement Project procurements for the period beginning June 1, 2024 and
  ending December 31, 2024.
  8E - STAFF REPORT

  8F.  City Manager - Approve Third Amendment to Amended and Restated Lease with
  South End Racquet and Health Club, Inc. for City-Owned Property Located at
  2800 Skypark Drive. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council approve a third amendment to the
  amended and restated lease with the South End Racquet and Health Club, Inc. of Torrance,
  CA (C-1990) for City-owned property located at 2800 Skypark Drive, to consolidate the
  original lease into one comprehensive document and set forth certain agreements
  concerning the second Fair Market Valuation Period effective July 1, 2024.
  8F- STAFF REPORT

*The following item was added on Thursday, June 27, 2024.

  8G. Community Services - Approve Expenditure Increase to City-County Municipal
  Services Agreement for Sole Source Animal Care and Control Services.
  Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed $100,000 (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council approve an
  expenditure increase to the city-county municipal services agreement (C2019-043) with the
  County of Los Angeles Department of Animal Care and Control in the amount of $100,000,
  for a new not-to-exceed amount of $785,000, to provide sole source animal care and control
  services for the period beginning July 1, 2023 and ending June 30, 2024.
  8G - STAFF REPORT

9.  ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS

  9A. Transit – Award Contract Services Agreement for Unarmed Security Services.
  Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed $1,708,640.85 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Transit Director that City Council award a contract services
  agreement to Nationwide Guard Services, Inc. of Rancho Cucamonga, CA (RFP B2024-05)
  for an amount not-to-exceed $1,708,640.85 to provide unarmed security services for the
   Transit Department for a three-year period beginning July 1, 2024 and ending June 30,
  2027.
  9A - STAFF REPORT

  9B. City Attorney – Approve Second Amendment to Fee Agreement for Legal
  Services. Expenditure: $216,000 (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the City Attorney that City Council approve a second amendment to the
  fee agreement with law firm Liebert Cassidy Whitmore of Los Angeles (C2023-114) in the
  amount of $216,000, for a new not-to-exceed amount of $466,000, to provide the City with
  legal services pertaining to Civil Litigation Matter Blake Williams vs. City of Torrance.
  9B - STAFF REPORT

  9C. Transit – Approve Metro ExpressLanes Net Toll Reinvestment Grant Funding
  Agreement with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
  (LACMTA) and Appropriate Funds for Line 4X. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Transit Director that City Council:
  1) Approve Metro ExpressLanes Net Toll Reinvestment Grant Funding Agreement
  #920000000MX202320 with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
  Authority (LACMTA) for incremental transit service on the I-110 Harbor freeway; and
  2) Upon execution of Agreement #920000000MX202320, appropriate $3,220,000 to a
  newly created Grant Project for incremental transit service on the I-110 Harbor freeway.
  9C - STAFF REPORT

  9D. Transit – Approve Metro ExpressLanes Net Toll Reinvestment Grant Funding
  Agreements with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
  (LACMTA) and Appropriate Funds for Line 1 and Line 6. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Transit Director that City Council:
  1) Approve Metro ExpressLanes Net Toll Reinvestment Grant Funding Agreement
  #920000000MX202305 with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Authority (LACMTA)
  for the Line 1 Service Enhancement project; and
  2) Upon execution of Agreement #920000000MX202305, appropriate $3,066,435 to a
  newly created Grant Project for the Line 1 Service Enhancement project; and
  3) Approve Metro ExpressLanes Net Toll Reinvestment Grant Funding Agreement
  #920000000MX202309 with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
  Authority (LACMTA) for the Line 6 Service Enhancement and Expansion to Dignity
  Health Sport Park project; and
  4) Upon execution of Agreement #920000000MX202309, appropriate $3,693,874 to a
  newly created Grant Project for the Line 6 Service Enhancement and Expansion to
  Dignity Health Sports Park project.
  9D - STAFF REPORT

*The following item was added on Thursday, June 27, 2024.

  9E.  City Clerk, City Manager, and City Attorney - Adopt RESOLUTIONS Calling 2024
  Special Municipal Election on November 5, 2024 Regarding Amendments to City
  Charter. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk, City Manager, and City Attorney that City Council: 1)
  Adopt a RESOLUTION calling a Special Municipal Election on November 5, 2024 for the
  purpose of submitting proposed City Charter amendments to a vote of the qualified electors
  of the City of Torrance; and 2) Adopt a RESOLUTION requesting the Los Angeles County
  Board of Supervisors to agree to consolidate the election on the Statewide General Election
  Ballot; and 3) Give direction to the City Clerk on whether the City Council would like to
  select a letter or letters for the ballot measure.
  9E - STAFF REPORT
  9E - MATERIAL AVAILABLE
  9E - SUPPLEMENTAL
  9E - SUPPLEMENTAL #2

10.  HEARINGS

  10A. Community Development – Conduct Public Hearing on Substantial Amendment
  to Five-Year Consolidated Plan Covering Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-27 and Annual
  Action Plan Covering FY 2024-25, Approve and Authorize Submission of
  Substantial Amendment to FY 2023-27 Consolidated Plan and FY 2024-25 Action
   Plan, and Authorize City Manager to Execute Documents. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1) Conduct a public hearing and take public testimony on the Substantial Amendment to
  the Five-Year Consolidated Plan covering the period July 1, 2023 – June 30, 2028, and
  the Annual Action Plan covering the period July 1, 2024 – June 30, 2025; and
  2) Approve and authorize submission of Substantial Amendment to the FY 2023-27
  Consolidated Plan and FY 2024-25 Action Plan to the U.S. Department of Housing and
  Urban Development (HUD); and
  3) Authorize the City Manager to execute all appropriate and necessary documents to
  receive funding and implement approved uses.
  10A - STAFF REPORT

  10B. Finance – Conduct Public Hearing and Adopt RESOLUTIONS Authorizing and
  Directing Los Angeles County Assessor to Include Delinquent Solid Waste,
  Sewer Discharge, and Water Usage Fees as a Special Assessment. Expenditure:
  None.
  Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council:
  1) Conduct a public hearing; and
  2) Adopt a RESOLUTION authorizing and directing the Los Angeles County Assessor to
  include delinquent solid waste fees as a special assessment to be collected at the
  same time and in the same manner as county taxes; and
  3) Adopt a RESOLUTION authorizing and directing the Los Angeles County Assessor to
  include delinquent sewer discharge fees as a special assessment to be collected at the
  same time and in the same manner as county taxes; and
  4) Adopt a RESOLUTION authorizing and directing the Los Angeles County Assessor to
  include delinquent water usage fees as a special assessment to be collected at the
  same time and in the same manner as county taxes.
  10B - STAFF REPORT

11.  AGENCY AGENDAS –– None Scheduled.

12.  2ND READING ORDINANCES – None Scheduled.

13.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #2 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) Council Order –
  Gerson, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Sheikh, Mayor Chen This portion of the meeting
  is reserved for comments on items not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act,
  City Council cannot act on items raised during public comment, but may respond
  briefly to statements made or questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item
  to staff. Speakers under Orals are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral
  Communications #2 and no longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you
  step up to the microphone. If presenting handout material to Council, please provide
  11 copies to the City Clerk before speaking. Handouts will be distributed while you
  speak.

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  15A. Adjournment of City Council meeting to Tuesday, July 16, 2024, at 5:00 p.m. for
  closed session in the West Annex Commission Meeting Room. Tuesday, July 9,
  2024, is a Council Dark Night.
  15A - STAFF REPORT
